name: @appstrate/twenty-mcp
description: Twenty CRM integration backed by Twenty's own MCP server ({server}/mcp), for Twenty Cloud (api.twenty.com) and for any self-hosted server: the server URL is a connection variable, so one package serves every deployment and each connection reaches only its own. The sidecar opens a Streamable HTTP MCP client and injects the selected credential as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Two interchangeable auths. (1) OAuth, chosen per connection against the server the user named: RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery on the rendered MCP URL, whose authorization server must be that server's origin, RFC 8414 metadata, RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration as a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`), RFC 7636 PKCE (S256) and the RFC 9207 `iss` response parameter, one client per server and space; the `api` scope reaches the workspace data and `profile` the user's identity, and Twenty issues a refresh token with every authorization code. (2) API key — a workspace key created under Settings → APIs & Webhooks, whose access is the role it is assigned. Twenty's MCP is a tool catalogue rather than one tool per object: `get_tool_catalog` and `learn_tools` describe the workspace's tools — generated from its own data model, custom objects included — and `execute_tool` runs one of them, so every record operation goes through `execute_tool` and the role behind the credential is the only bound on it. `allow_undeclared_tools` lets an agent take whatever a server's version advertises.

base_url.title: URL du serveur Twenty
base_url.description: Adresse de l'API de votre serveur, sans chemin (ex. https://crm.example.com) ; gardez https://api.twenty.com pour Twenty Cloud.

scope_catalog.label: Workspace data
scope_catalog.description: Read and write the workspace's records and metadata through the MCP server, within the user's role.

api_key.title: Clé d'API
api_key.description: Clé créée dans Settings → APIs & Webhooks → Create key, affichée une seule fois. Elle agit avec le rôle qui lui est attribué (Settings → Members → Roles) : choisissez-en un qui limite ce que l'agent peut lire et modifier.
